docs.title: pensieve-traces
docs.text:
Claude Code (and other agents) record every session as raw JSONL. Those files hold far more than the conversation: file-history backups, full API request blobs, cost state and UI flags, plus whatever secrets, paths and private code passed through the session. claude.ai chats can be exported as a data export (conversations.json). pensieve-traces reads both into one canonical session model, redacts them, and writes:

Output What it is Status STS Hugging Face Session Trace Simple Format: one JSONL file per session, viewable on the Hub as an agent trace available (convert --to sts) OpenRouter Broadcast One JSON file per model request, with tokens and cost planned ConvoMem conversations Sessions as {id, messages[{speaker, text}]} conversations, one persona per project, ready to be used as history or filler available (convert --to convomem-conversations) ConvoMem dataset Questions, answers and evidence messages generated by a model from Claude Code sessions and claude.ai chats, in the ConvoMem layout that convomem-arena reads (running convomem-arena on a local folder needs convomem-arena#18) available (build convomem, check-convomem) 
readers                 canonical model                 outputs
claude_code ─┐          Session                       ┌─ STS writer
claude_ai   ─┤
codex (later)├─────►      messages: id, parent_id,  ──┼─ OpenRouter writer
pi (later)  ─┘            timestamp, role, text,      ├─ ConvoMem conversations
                          reasoning, tool calls,      └─ ConvoMem Q/A builder
                          model, request_id, usage
                        + redaction (on by default)

Privacy

Traces can contain prompts, tool output, local paths, secrets, private code and personal data. Redaction is on by default, but review anything before you publish it, and keep datasets private when unsure.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Install, then convert Claude Code sessions or a claude.ai export, or build a ConvoMem dataset.
  • Redaction and privacy: what is replaced and what is not.
  • CLI reference and Python API.

Created by Sajjadur Rahman · rahmansunny071@gmail.com

docs.title: Canonical model
docs.text:
pensieve_traces.model defines the harness-neutral dataclasses Session, Message, ToolCall, Usage and the Role enum (no extra dependencies). Timestamps are timezone-aware, tool arguments stay a raw JSON string, and Session.to_json() / Session.from_json() round-trip losslessly. The model holds raw text and does no redaction.

from pathlib import Path

from pensieve_traces import Session

session = Session.from_json(Path("session.json").read_text())
session.tool_result_for("call-1")

Every reader and writer goes through this model; formats are never converted directly into each other. See the diagram on the Overview.

docs.title: STS
docs.text: STS is the Hugging Face Session Trace Simple Format: one JSONL file per session, named <session id>.jsonl, viewable on the Hub as an agent trace. Write it with pensieve-traces convert --to sts (Claude Code, claude.ai); the options and the fields STS has no place for are listed there. convert writes the header key pensieveRedacted (true when redaction ran, false with --no-redact), which upload checks. Exports from claude.ai carry harness: "claude.ai" in the header.

docs.title: ConvoMem conversations
docs.text:
pensieve-traces convert --to convomem-conversations exports a project's sessions as ConvoMem-style conversations (one session per conversation, ordered by start time), in the filler-file layout convomem-arena reads (loading them from a local folder needs convomem-arena#18):

pensieve-traces convert path/to/<project-dir> --to convomem-conversations --out convomem/
pensieve-traces convert path/to/claude-export --to convomem-conversations --out convomem/

Input is detected as for STS (a claude.ai export gives one conversation per chat; --from overrides).

--out is a directory and receives two files:

  • conversations.json: {"evidence_items": [{"conversations": [{"id", "containsEvidence", "messages": [{"speaker", "text"}]}]}]} (the filler-file layout; id is the session id, speakers are User / Assistant).
  • conversations.message_ids.json: {conversation id: [canonical message id, ...]}, index-aligned with each conversation's messages, so Q/A generation can point evidence at exact messages.

Only user prompts and assistant prose are kept; meta, sidechain, system and tool-result messages and empty turns are dropped. Assistant tool calls become one-line [ran Bash: git status] summaries (from Python, tool_activity="drop" omits them). Redaction is on by default, as for STS, and one anonymizer covers all sessions. The command refuses (writing nothing) if either output file already exists or --out would overwrite the input sessions. From Python: see the Python API.

docs.title: ConvoMem dataset layout
docs.text:
build convomem writes, in --out:

  • core_benchmark/evidence_questions/<category folder>/<N>_evidence/me.json, with folders user_evidence, assistant_facts_evidence, changing_evidence, abstention_evidence, preference_evidence, implicit_connection_evidence (folders without items are not created). Each item has question, answer, message_evidences and conversations (all containsEvidence: true).
  • core_benchmark/filler_conversations/me.json: the conversations that are evidence for no item. convomem-arena's mixer leaves an item's own evidence out of its filler, but its data check does not, so keeping evidence conversations in the filler file would make most items flag there. The cost is a smaller filler pool.
  • build_manifest.json: input and conversation counts (no paths), model name, prompt hashes, whether redaction was on, per-category item counts and the drop counts of each step. No base URL, key or timestamp.

Check the structure with check-convomem.

docs.title: Reading Claude Code sessions
docs.text:
pensieve_traces.readers.claude_code turns raw Claude Code JSONL into canonical sessions (stdlib only). Only the conversation is kept: user, assistant and system records, plus the ai-title as Session.title. File backups, API request blobs, cost state and every other record type are skipped, and toolUseResult is never read.

from pensieve_traces.readers.claude_code import read_project, read_session

session = read_session("path/to/<session>.jsonl")
sessions = read_project("path/to/project-dir")  # *.jsonl; subagent files merge into their session

Records sharing a requestId stay separate messages; token usage is attached only to the last one so sums are not double-counted. Malformed input raises ClaudeCodeParseError with the file path and line number. The reader does no redaction.

docs.title: Reading claude.ai exports
docs.text:
pensieve_traces.readers.claude_ai turns a claude.ai data export (Settings, Privacy, Export data) into canonical sessions, one per conversation (stdlib only). It reads only conversations.json; the account block, memories, projects, artifacts, light_metadata and the manifest (which holds signed download URLs) are never opened. pensieve-traces convert accepts exports too (see Convert a claude.ai export).

from pensieve_traces.readers.claude_ai import read_export

sessions = read_export("path/to/export-dir")  # or path/to/conversations.json
  • Sessions have harness="claude.ai" and come back in file order. There is no model name or token usage in the export.
  • Text is built from the content blocks (the top-level text is unreliable). A human turn becomes a user message; each injected_prompt_block (system notes such as the memory header) becomes its own is_meta message. An assistant turn with interleaved thinking, tool calls and results is split, in order, into assistant and tool messages.
  • Branches (edited or regenerated turns): only the path to the latest message is kept, and Session.metadata["dropped_branch_messages"] counts the rest.
  • Attached files and images become placeholders such as [attached: name.pdf]. Attachment text is dropped unless you pass include_attachments=True. Web results, image galleries and local resources in tool output are summarised in one line, not copied as JSON.
  • Malformed input raises ClaudeAiParseError with the file path and a location such as conversations[3].chat_messages[7]. The reader does no redaction, and injected prompt text, thinking and tool output stay in the sessions, so redact before sharing.

docs.title: Redaction and privacy
docs.text:
Privacy

Traces can contain prompts, tool output, local paths, secrets, private code and personal data. Redaction is on by default, but review anything before you publish it, and keep datasets private when unsure.

Install the optional extra to enable redaction: pip install "pensieve-traces[redact] @ git+https://github.com/rahmansunny071/pensieve-traces@v0.1.0" (uses teich's TraceAnonymizer; the base install has no dependencies).

from pensieve_traces import prepare_for_output, redact_session

safe = prepare_for_output(session)  # redacts by default; raises if teich is missing
raw = prepare_for_output(session, redact=False)  # explicit opt-out, emits a UserWarning
copy = redact_session(session)  # scrubbed deep copy, input untouched

build convomem also redacts through prepare_for_output, once over all inputs, before any model call. Writers must obtain their session through prepare_for_output. It never falls back to unredacted output: without the extra it raises RedactionUnavailableError. Ids, tool names, timestamps and usage are left as is. Redaction is pattern-based and best-effort, so review output before sharing.

docs.title: What redaction covers on chat content
docs.text:
teich was tuned on coding sessions. Measured on redact_session (teich 0.3.8, the version uv.lock pins, plus a small pre-pass that also replaces an email address directly followed by a period) on a synthetic claude.ai-style chat (tests/fixtures/redact/chat_pii_session.json), pinned by tests/test_redact_chat_coverage.py so a teich upgrade that changes coverage shows up as a test change:

Kind Replaced email address, also when followed by ., .), .", a curly quote, !, ?, : or ; yes dashed SSN-style number (987-65-4320) yes street address after "I live at" yes 10-digit phone after a phrase like "Call me at" yes undashed SSN-style number (My SSN is 987654320.) no street address after other phrasing ("Send it to 42 Maple Lane, Springfield.") no 7-digit phone after other phrasing ("My phone is 555-0143") no IBAN no card number no person name no health detail no money amount no

Not covered: an address followed by a period and then a letter, digit, -, _, % or + with no space (name@host.invalid.I will, .5, .2024, .-x), which teich also misses. Phone and address matching depends on the surrounding phrasing (teich 0.3.8 replaces an address only after phrases like "I live at" or "address:"; "My address is …", "Send it to …" and "Deliver to …" are left as is). Redaction does not catch chat personal data in general: review claude.ai traces before sharing them.

docs.title: Convert a claude.ai export
docs.text:
Export your chats from claude.ai (Settings, Privacy, Export data), then point convert at the export directory or its conversations.json:

pip install "pensieve-traces[redact] @ git+https://github.com/rahmansunny071/pensieve-traces@v0.1.0"
pensieve-traces convert path/to/claude-export --to sts --out traces/
pensieve-traces convert path/to/claude-export --to convomem-conversations --out convomem/

Input is detected as for Claude Code sessions; --from claude-ai forces the claude.ai reader. Exports write one <conversation uuid>.jsonl per conversation with harness: "claude.ai" in the header; attachment text is left out. A claude.ai export gives one ConvoMem conversation per chat. The Hub's rendering of the claude.ai harness id is unverified (STS only lists llama.app).

--out equal to the export directory, inside it, or equal to the directory of a conversations.json input is refused, as for Claude Code input. What the reader keeps and drops is described under Readers.

Chats hold personal data

Redaction does not catch chat personal data in general (names, health details, money amounts, card numbers and more). See Redaction and privacy and review claude.ai traces before sharing them.

docs.title: Convert Claude Code sessions
docs.text:
pensieve-traces convert turns a Claude Code session file or project directory, or a claude.ai export, into STS JSONL for the Hugging Face trace viewer, one <session id>.jsonl per session (stdlib only):

pip install "pensieve-traces[redact] @ git+https://github.com/rahmansunny071/pensieve-traces@v0.1.0"
pensieve-traces convert path/to/<project-dir> --to sts --out traces/
  • Input is detected: a directory of *.jsonl files or one session file is Claude Code. A directory with conversations.json and no *.jsonl (or a file named conversations.json) is a claude.ai export. A directory holding both is refused as ambiguous, and one holding neither is an error. --from claude-code or --from claude-ai forces the reader.
  • Redaction is on by default. Without the redact extra the command exits with an error and writes nothing; pass --no-redact to write unredacted output (a warning is printed).
  • --out must not be the input directory (or inside it), nor the directory of an input file (for an export, its directory): Claude Code names sessions <session id>.jsonl, so writing there would overwrite the originals. The command refuses and writes nothing.
  • Sidechain (subagent) messages are skipped; add --include-sidechains to keep them.
  • Fields STS has no place for are dropped: parent ids, usage, request ids, is_meta/is_error flags, metadata, cwd, project, branch and session start/end times. Meta messages are still written.

For ConvoMem conversations, use --to convomem-conversations (see Output formats). From Python, see the Python API.

docs.title: Build a ConvoMem dataset
docs.text:
pensieve-traces build convomem turns Claude Code sessions and claude.ai chats, together, into a ConvoMem-style memory dataset about you (one persona, me): a model finds facts in your conversations and writes questions and answers across ConvoMem's six categories, and code checks that the evidence is verbatim.

pip install "pensieve-traces[redact] @ git+https://github.com/rahmansunny071/pensieve-traces@v0.1.0"
pensieve-traces build convomem path/to/<project-dir> path/to/claude-export \
  --out dataset/ --model qwen3:14b [--topics topics.json]
  • Inputs: one or more, in any mix (a Claude Code project directory or session file, a claude.ai export directory or conversations.json), detected as for convert (--from forces one reader for all inputs). Sessions with the same id across inputs are read once (the first wins).
  • Model endpoint: any OpenAI-compatible server, by default a local Ollama (--base-url http://localhost:11434/v1). --api-key-env NAME names the environment variable holding a key (never a flag; the command fails early if it is unset). A --base-url that is not localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] is refused unless --allow-remote-model is given, and a URL with embedded credentials is always refused. Before the first model call the command prints which endpoint receives the text. The command never contacts the Hub; uploading stays a separate, explicit upload run.
  • Redaction is on by default and runs once, with one anonymizer, over all inputs before any text reaches the model, so placeholders are consistent across conversations, evidence and filler. It is best-effort: see Redaction and privacy for what it misses (names, health details and money amounts in chats, for example). Without the redact extra the command exits with an error and writes nothing; --no-redact sends and writes unredacted text and prints a warning. Sessions are redacted in input order, so adding or reordering inputs can change placeholders and miss part of the cache.
  • Output: see Output formats.
  • Topics (optional): see Topics.
  • Where things go: the dataset is written to a temporary directory beside --out and moved into place, so a failed run leaves nothing half-written. The command refuses an --out that is, or is inside, an input, that is a file, or that already holds core_benchmark/ or build_manifest.json, and it never replaces an existing file. The model reply cache lives beside the dataset in <out>.cache/ (or --cache-dir), so sharing the dataset folder never ships model outputs; the cache directory is refused inside an input or inside --out. A rerun reuses the cache.

Privacy

The dataset is about you: it holds facts from your conversations. Review it before sharing, keep it private, and remember that redaction is pattern-based (see the table in Redaction and privacy). The cache holds model replies about your conversations too.

Then check the dataset. From Python: pensieve_traces.builders.convomem (extract_candidates, build_items) and dataset; see the Python API.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pensieve-traces is not on PyPI. It installs from GitHub, pinned to the v0.1.0 release tag, so every command below names the repository URL.

The base install has no dependencies:

pip install "pensieve-traces @ git+https://github.com/rahmansunny071/pensieve-traces@v0.1.0"

Optional extras go in the brackets:

pip install "pensieve-traces[redact] @ git+https://github.com/rahmansunny071/pensieve-traces@v0.1.0"   # redaction (uses teich); needed by convert and build
pip install "pensieve-traces[hub] @ git+https://github.com/rahmansunny071/pensieve-traces@v0.1.0"      # upload to the Hugging Face Hub
pip install "pensieve-traces[docs] @ git+https://github.com/rahmansunny071/pensieve-traces@v0.1.0"     # build this documentation site

With uv, the same source installs the CLI as a tool or into the current environment:

uv tool install "pensieve-traces[redact] @ git+https://github.com/rahmansunny071/pensieve-traces@v0.1.0"
uv pip install "pensieve-traces[redact] @ git+https://github.com/rahmansunny071/pensieve-traces@v0.1.0"

Install the redact extra to enable redaction: it uses teich's TraceAnonymizer. Redaction is on by default, so without the extra convert and build convomem exit with an error and write nothing (see Redaction and privacy).

To work on the code instead, see Development.

docs.title: Checking a ConvoMem dataset
docs.text:
pensieve-traces check-convomem dataset/

The structure check needs no extra dependency, reads only dataset/ and writes nothing. It prints the files and items per category folder, then every problem as file[item i]: reason, and exits 1 if there is any problem (0 and ok otherwise). It checks that:

  • only known category folders and <N>_evidence folders with N in that category's range exist;
  • every evidence file is {"evidence_items": [...]} and each item has a non-empty question, answer and conversations, and message_evidences of length N;
  • each message_evidences[].text is, verbatim, a message of the item's conversations, and the evidence comes from distinct conversations (as many as the conversations marked containsEvidence);
  • changing_evidence evidence appears in conversation order;
  • each evidence file has a filler file of the same name, and no evidence conversation is in it.

From Python: pensieve_traces.builders.convomem.check_dataset(path) returns a list of Problem(file, item, reason). Content checks (answer grounding, duplicates, filler contamination) are not done here: they belong to convomem-arena's data check. Once convomem-arena#18 lands, that check and the taskset can run on a local folder: run python -m convomem_arena.data_check --local dataset/ --out reports/, and point the taskset at dataset/ as its local root (see #18 for the setting). Until then they read only the Hub dataset.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text:
build convomem --topics topics.json maps a topic name to local matchers:

{"home-care": {"titles": ["caregiver"], "projects": ["demo"], "ids": []}}

ids match a session id exactly, projects the project name (the basename of the session's working directory; claude.ai chats have none) and titles a case-insensitive substring of the title. Matching conversations get "topic": [...] and items "topics": [...] (the union over their evidence conversations), extra keys convomem-arena ignores; no model labels topics. A malformed file is an error before any model call.

docs.title: Uploading to the Hub
docs.text:
pensieve-traces upload pushes converted traces to a Hugging Face dataset, private by default. Uploading is always intentional: upload is the only command that contacts the Hub, and convert and every other command only write local files. It needs the optional extra and your own login (hf auth login); the tool never asks for, stores or prints a token.

pip install "pensieve-traces[hub] @ git+https://github.com/rahmansunny071/pensieve-traces@v0.1.0"
pensieve-traces upload traces/ --repo <user>/<dataset>   # private unless --public
  • convert writes the STS header key pensieveRedacted (true when redaction ran, false with --no-redact). upload refuses any file whose first line lacks "pensieveRedacted": true (a missing marker counts as unredacted) unless you pass --allow-unredacted. The marker is an attestation, not proof; review traces before sharing.
  • Only the top-level *.jsonl files of the directory are uploaded, at the repo root.
  • If any file has "harness": "claude.ai" in its header, upload prints a warning with their count before the confirmation prompt (also with --yes) saying redaction does not catch names, health details, money amounts or card and bank account numbers and catches only some addresses and phone numbers. It never refuses on this basis; see Redaction and privacy for the measured coverage.
  • A summary (file count, total size, repo, visibility) is shown and you are asked to confirm; --yes skips the prompt.
  • --public must be explicit and prints a warning. If the repo already exists and is public, the upload is refused unless --public is given. Without the hub extra the command prints an install hint and exits 1.

• Installs come from GitHub, pinned to the release tag; the package is not on PyPI; __version__ reads the installed version; install hints point at GitHub (#86).
  • Repository scaffold and agent factory (CLAUDE.md, factory commands, workflows, CI).
  • Canonical session model (Session, Message, ToolCall, Usage, Role) with lossless JSON round-trip (#1).
  • Claude Code reader (read_session, read_project) from raw session JSONL to the canonical Session (#2).
  • Redaction pass on by default (redact_session, prepare_for_output, optional pensieve-traces[redact] extra using teich) (#3).
  • STS writer (write_session, session_to_sts_lines) and pensieve-traces convert --to sts CLI (#4).
  • pensieve-traces upload to a private Hugging Face dataset (optional pensieve-traces[hub] extra); STS writer adds the pensieveRedacted header key (#6).
  • convert refuses an --out directory that would overwrite the input session files (#36).
  • ConvoMem conversations export (convert --to convomem-conversations, write_conversations, sessions_to_conversations) with a message-ID map (#5).
  • README states that uploading is always intentional: only pensieve-traces upload contacts the Hub.
  • Factory skill updated to agent-factory v0.6.0 (docs-with-code rule and Documentation tech-debt tracker; ready-to-merge hand-off when a merge is refused, agent-factory#32); new factory:ready-to-merge label.
  • Factory skill synced to agent-factory v0.8.0 with its new sync-root-factory skill (version marker .claude/skills/factory/VERSION), plus the factory-lesson skill; the Reality check now reads a Real data: line from CLAUDE.md (missing means never).
  • claude.ai export reader (pensieve_traces.readers.claude_ai.read_export, ClaudeAiParseError) from conversations.json to canonical Sessions; README intro, readers diagram and STS status row updated (#46, #44).
  • ConvoMem builder 1/3: OpenAICompatibleClient (stdlib, local Ollama by default) and extract_candidates find candidate memory facts in conversations, with a per-window cache; prompts adapted from Salesforce ConvoMem (Apache-2.0, NOTICE) (#8).
  • convert accepts a claude.ai export (directory or conversations.json) for sts and convomem-conversations; input is auto-detected, --from {claude-code,claude-ai} overrides, load_sessions is the reusable loader; --out inside an export directory is refused (#47).
  • ConvoMem builder 2/3: build_items turns candidate facts into evidence items (question, answer, verbatim evidence) for the six ConvoMem categories, with code checks (one conversation per evidence message, verbatim evidence, chronology, duplicate questions, convomem-arena's filler check) and model verification with ConvoMem's judge prompts; every model call is cached; shared reply parsing and cache moved to builders/convomem/_common.py (#54).
  • Redaction coverage on chat personal data is measured and pinned (tests/test_redact_chat_coverage.py, README "Redaction" table, teich 0.3.8); upload warns before the confirmation prompt, also with --yes, how many files are claude.ai chats and what redaction does not catch; new upload.count_harness (#48).
  • ConvoMem builder 3/3: pensieve-traces build convomem INPUT... --out DIR --model M builds a ConvoMem dataset (evidence items for six categories, filler without evidence conversations, build_manifest.json) from Claude Code sessions and claude.ai exports in any mix; one redaction pass before any model call, local-only endpoint unless --allow-remote-model, optional --topics, cache beside the dataset, no-clobber output (builders/convomem/dataset.py, topics.py) (#55).
  • pensieve-traces check-convomem DIR and builders.convomem.check_dataset(path) -> list[Problem] check the structure of a generated ConvoMem dataset (category and count folders, verbatim evidence from distinct conversations, changing-evidence order, filler without evidence conversations); README documents running convomem-arena's full check once convomem-arena#18 lands (#9).
  • Redaction replaces an email address directly followed by a period (teich 0.3.8 left mail a@b.invalid. unredacted) with the same placeholder as the bare address, in text, metadata keys and values and tool arguments (_EmailPeriodGuard in redact.py); README "Redaction" table and pinned coverage rows updated (#67).
  • README: the ConvoMem dataset row says local-folder runs need convomem-arena#18, and the factory intro matches opt-in merges by the factory skill (#74).
  • README: ConvoMem conversations no longer claim convomem-arena loads them from a local folder today (needs convomem-arena#18) (#77).
  • README: new "Letting the factory merge for you" subsection (the heading the factory skill points to) holds the opt-in merge permission rule (#79).
  • Documentation site at https://rahmansunny071.github.io/pensieve-traces/ (MkDocs Material: mkdocs.yml, docs/, overrides/), published to gh-pages by the new .github/workflows/docs.yml; new optional docs extra (mkdocs-material); the README is now a landing page with a quick start, and the sections that moved are on the site (#81).
  • package metadata links the docs site (Documentation, Changelog in [project.urls]); the repo's About box links it too (#84).

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
pensieve-traces has four commands. The text below is each command's --help.

Command What it does Guide convert Convert session traces to STS or ConvoMem conversations Claude Code, claude.ai build convomem Build a ConvoMem dataset with a model Build a ConvoMem dataset check-convomem Check the structure of a generated dataset (reads only the directory) Checking upload Upload converted traces to a Hugging Face dataset (the only command that contacts the Hub) Uploading

Redaction is on by default for convert and build convomem; --no-redact turns it off with a warning.

docs.title: pensieve-traces --help
docs.text:
usage: pensieve-traces [-h] {convert,build,check-convomem,upload} ...

positional arguments:
  {convert,build,check-convomem,upload}
    convert             convert session traces to a shareable format
    build               build a dataset from session traces
    check-convomem      check the structure of a generated ConvoMem dataset
                        (reads only DIR)
    upload              upload converted traces to a Hugging Face dataset

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

docs.title: pensieve-traces convert --help
docs.text:
usage: pensieve-traces convert [-h] [--from {claude-code,claude-ai}]
                               --to {convomem-conversations,sts} --out OUT
                               [--no-redact] [--include-sidechains]
                               input

positional arguments:
  input                 a Claude Code session .jsonl file or project
                        directory, or a claude.ai export directory or
                        conversations.json

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --from {claude-code,claude-ai}
                        input source (default: detected from the input)
  --to {convomem-conversations,sts}
                        output format
  --out OUT             output directory (sts: one file per session; convomem-
                        conversations: two files)
  --no-redact           write unredacted output (redaction is the default)
  --include-sidechains  include subagent (sidechain) messages

docs.title: pensieve-traces build convomem --help
docs.text:
usage: pensieve-traces build convomem [-h] --out OUT --model MODEL
                                      [--base-url BASE_URL]
                                      [--api-key-env API_KEY_ENV]
                                      [--allow-remote-model] [--topics TOPICS]
                                      [--cache-dir CACHE_DIR]
                                      [--from {claude-code,claude-ai}]
                                      [--no-redact]
                                      input [input ...]

positional arguments:
  input                 Claude Code session files or project directories,

docs.title: How this repo is built: an agent factory
docs.text:
Work happens through an issue-driven factory, either on Claude Code GitHub Actions (below) or from a Claude Code session with the factory skill. Agents write short designs, review them, build, test and open PRs. In the Actions factory only the maintainer starts or advances work and merges to main; the factory skill merges on green gates only if the maintainer's permissions allow its gh pr merge … --admin command (see the permission rule below). No agent publishes a release or uploads anything.

  1. Open an issue with the Factory task template.
  2. Add factory:design. The design agent writes .factory/designs/issue-N.md and opens a draft design PR.
  3. Review it; iterate with @claude … comments or edit it yourself.
  4. Add design:approved to the design PR. The build agent implements it on factory/issue-N, runs the checks until green and opens a PR.
  5. The review agent checks the PR against the design and CLAUDE.md.
  6. Merge. Releases stay manual.
Label Applied by Meaning factory:design maintainer, on an issue Ask an agent for a design factory:designing agent Design in progress / awaiting review design:approved maintainer, on the design PR Signed off: start building factory:building agent Implementation in progress factory:review agent Implementation PR open, awaiting merge factory:blocked agent Agent hit something it shouldn't decide factory:ready-to-merge factory skill Every gate passed but the merge was refused: you merge it

Agent rules live in CLAUDE.md; the stage prompts in .claude/commands/.

The factory skill (.claude/skills/factory/) runs the same pipeline from a Claude Code session. Two of its rules:

  • Docs ship with the code: every PR updates the docs its change affects, and its Handoff says which (or why none). Older mismatches become sub-issues of the "Documentation tech-debt" issue (#43).
  • Ready to merge: if every gate passes but the merge is refused (the harness denies it or GitHub rejects it), the skill never works around it. It labels the PR factory:ready-to-merge, comments the exact merge command and carries on; queue.py and the end-of-run report list what waits for you. To let it merge by itself instead, see Letting the factory merge for you.

Two companion skills ship with it. sync-root-factory (.claude/skills/sync-root-factory/) brings the factory skill up to the latest agent-factory release as a PR ("sync the factory to the latest release"); the version this repo is on is in .claude/skills/factory/VERSION. factory-lesson (.claude/skills/factory-lesson/) files a factory problem as a lesson issue in agent-factory ("file a factory lesson: …"), after one confirmation and with no real data in the text.

docs.title: Letting the factory merge for you
docs.text:
Add this permission rule yourself, to .claude/settings.local.json (keep it out of git) or ~/.claude/settings.json, not to the committed .claude/settings.json. It lets the factory skill run its merge command with your ruleset bypass (--admin), which it needs because a PR's author can't approve their own PR. Because it hands an agent your bypass, the repo doesn't ship it:

{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(gh pr merge * --merge --admin --delete-branch)"] } }

The rule matches only commands that start with gh pr merge and end in exactly --merge --admin --delete-branch, which is how the skill runs the merge (a trailing -R isn't covered). The skill still merges only when every gate passes, and never works around a refused merge.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Redaction is best-effort. It is pattern-based and misses names, health details, money amounts, card numbers, IBANs and undashed SSN-style numbers in chats, and some addresses and phone numbers. See the measured coverage.
  • Email followed by a period and then text with no space (name@host.invalid.I will) is not covered.
  • The Hub's rendering of the claude.ai harness id is unverified (STS only lists llama.app).
  • OpenRouter Broadcast output is planned, not available. Other agent readers (codex, pi) are later.
  • ConvoMem conversations and datasets are not loadable by convomem-arena from a local folder yet: that needs convomem-arena#18. check-convomem checks structure only; content checks belong to convomem-arena's data check.
  • Fields STS has no place for are dropped (parent ids, usage, request ids, flags, metadata, cwd, project, branch, session times).
  • The pensieveRedacted marker is an attestation, not proof.
  • Branches in claude.ai chats: only the path to the latest message is kept.
